openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Wednesday’s gate is rain — not the admin stack. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Own the threshold from the first breath.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a dry sky to start. Fierce calm is Wednesday composure under a washout: charge first, body second, two must-dos, quiet admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Wednesday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Rain outside; tempo inside. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Gnostics treated the visible world as a curtain, not a cage. A washout morning is practice: the sky hides the sun, not the light. What you cannot see still orders the day — so act from the current you already carry, not the clearance the weather withholds.

items.hed: Name the next move, not the whole map
items.body: Hermetic operators win by collapsing infinity into one executable step. Wednesday’s board is crowded; the esoteric move is smaller: one breath, one opener, one must-do. Mystery scales down into action.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.hed: Seal the day before you open it
grimoire.body: Solomon’s craft was not spectacle — it was order. Before the king spoke to spirits, he set the circle: a boundary that said what enters and what waits. Your Opening Bell is that circle. Breath marks the edge. Body fills the center. Only then do the desks, the inbox, and the ledger get a hearing. A day without a seal leaks; a sealed day obeys the will that drew it.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, say once under your breath: ‘This threshold is mine.’ Then start the 3-minute opener. Do not check mail until both are done.

lesson.oneLiner: Stop hunting random AI apps — keep a four-layer discovery stack and open one layer when you need a tool.
beats: Layer 1 — directories: Future Tools, There’s An AI For That, aitools.fyi when you don’t know what exists.
Layer 2 — try-before-build: Hugging Face Spaces + Replicate to test models without standing up infra.
Layer 3 — make: Runway / Leonardo / Ideogram / Suno / ElevenLabs when the output is media, not chat.
Layer 4 — ship craft: Gamma, Napkin, Excalidraw, Postman, carbon.now.sh for decks, diagrams, APIs, and clean screenshots.
Rule: bookmark the stack once; pick one layer per job so you don’t drown in tabs.
lesson.takeaway: Your moat isn’t more bookmarks — it’s a retrieval habit. @mmmik000: open Layer 1 only when stuck; otherwise go straight to try or ship.
